candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Preregister the trial with the same native account and next_action's frozen task, account and effect checks. Run it on WSL and on one macos-arm64 Mac, which is untested. Arms: the stack pin 2.1.284 against 2.1.291 or later (installed 2.1.292; skip 2.1.288 to 2.1.290), N>=5 per arm. Each trial starts a `claude --bg` session and a `claude -p --output-format stream-json` session, with a turn that issues a parallel tool batch including one MCP call. Kill the session with SIGKILL mid-turn, then resume it by id (`claude --resume <id>`, or `claude respawn` for --bg). Measure four things: the share of pre-kill turns present after resume, MCP call success after resume, duplicated or re-sent turns, and whether new assistant or usage entries reach the transcript after `claude stop <id>`. Move the pin only if the newer build keeps every pre-kill turn in every trial where 2.1.284 loses any, with no regression on the frozen checks. Otherwise keep 2.1.284 and record the outcome against gap 4. Any task-quality arm runs under Harbor or Inspect.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: FIRST-PARTY SURFACE OF THE WINNER, not a replacement. It covers the native app-server, its shared local daemon and the in-repo Python and TypeScript SDKs, all used through the existing ChatGPT sign-in. Gap 0's only receipt (gap-wave2 codex-resume-pinned-build.json) is N=1 on 0.155.1 and states that a later release needs its own trial. The stack now installs 0.160.0 and this host runs 0.160.1, where local sessions moved to paginated thread history (`codex migrate-rollouts`: 'Inspect or migrate legacy local sessions to paginated thread history'; rust-v0.159.0 #48151 item anchors for thread/items/list). Resuming a 0.155.1-era session on the current pin is therefore unqualified. open_gaps[4] has no follow-up. `codex exec --help` (0.160.1) lists only the resume, fork and review subcommands plus --json JSONL events, with no turn-interrupt or steer control, so cancellation there is a process signal. The vendor Python SDK `openai-codex` (sdk/python) reuses the existing Codex authentication, ChatGPT login included. It exposes per-turn stream(), steer() and interrupt(), thread_resume and thread_fork, and thread_list with cursors. The shared daemon (`codex app-server daemon`, `codex agents`) is a native session manager. The same SDK path is the agent-sdks layer's winner (component codex at 0.155.1), whose open gaps record no native cancel receipt and no multi-turn resume, so one preregistered trial feeds both layers. rust-v0.160.0 adds #49105 (unsent queued messages resume after reconnection without duplicate sends) and #49160 (saved permissions restored on resume). #49144, #49161 and #49171 fix TUI provider, reasoning-summary and verbosity settings, and which sessions the resume and fork history lists. They are not crash-durability fixes, contrary to the seed's grouping.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Preregister the trial with the same ChatGPT sign-in and next_action's frozen task, account and effect checks. Run it on WSL first, then on one macos-arm64 Mac, N>=5 per check. Check 1: resume a 0.155.1-era session on 0.160.1, before and after `codex migrate-rollouts`. It passes with the same thread id, every pre-upgrade turn returned by thread/items/list, and no lost turns. Check 2: SIGKILL the app-server daemon mid-turn, restart it, then thread_resume the same id. It passes when pre-kill items are retained and a queued message is delivered exactly once (#49105). Check 3: cancel a running turn with the SDK's interrupt() and, for comparison, SIGINT and SIGKILL of `codex exec --json`, with both arms on the same Codex build (the SDK pins openai-codex-cli-bin 0.153.4 by default). Measure seconds until events stop, and confirm that no further item or usage events follow the stop. Adopt the SDK/app-server path as this layer's programmatic surface only if it passes every check `codex exec --json` passes and also passes one of the cancellation or recovery checks that exec fails. Otherwise keep exec --json and record the results against gaps 0 and 4. Any task-quality arm runs under Harbor or Inspect.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: APM is a cross-client manifest and lockfile for the skills and instruction files this stack installs and records by hand. One apm.yml declares skills, instructions, agents, hooks, plugins and MCP servers. `apm install` deploys to Claude: skills to .claude/skills and instructions to .claude/rules/<name>.md, and the CLAUDE.md compile leaves out rules that are already deployed. It also deploys to Codex: .agents/skills plus .codex. The codex target has no instructions primitive and needs a separate root-context compile to AGENTS.md. apm.lock records resolved sources and content hashes. Every install scans for hidden Unicode. `apm audit` rebuilds the context in scratch and diffs it against the tree. It also exports an SBOM, and the README offers a drop-in replacement for `npx skills add`. The stack today runs vercel-labs/skills 1.7.0 global installs plus a hand-kept adoption/skills/manifest.json (pins, hashes, exclusions). That is glue an upstream now provides. APM does not decide what loads per task (the native client surfaces do that). Claude Code's native claude-md-and-agents-md mode also removes most of its instruction-sync value for these two clients. It is therefore a comparison against dyoshikawa/rulesync (keep_but_compare, 2026-10-06) and the vercel CLI, not a trial against the winners now. Unknown: whether the claude target maps package applyTo globs to `paths:`. The retrieved targets matrix documents that mapping only for antigravity. Supply-chain facts: 3 published repository advisories, all from May 2026: GHSA-xhrw-5qxx-jpwr (high: plugin.json component paths escape the plugin root during install), GHSA-q5pp-gvjg-h7v4 (high: symlinks are dereferenced during install) and GHSA-mq5j-pw29-jcv3 (medium: Windows tar path overwrite). Fixed versions were not checked here. Maintenance: v0.33.0 on 2026-10-02 and a default-branch commit on 2026-10-06.

It runs each case 3 times by default, supports free and LLM graders and a cost ceiling, and writes JSON and HTML reports. Under with-without, a `tool_used: Skill` grader becomes a with-only 'plugin-fired indicator'. That shows whether the skill fired in the top-level run; it does not test what a worker sees listed. The stack has no retained skill-arm fixture today. The value is stored as pluginConfigs["cc-plugin-agents-md@builtin"].options.instructionFiles and is read only from user, --settings or managed settings, never from project or local settings. The ID was agents-md@builtin before 2.1.285, so the stack's 2.1.284 pin uses the old ID. The stack keeps four hand-written `@AGENTS.md` shims (root, adoption/scaffold, blueprints/us-equities, blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery), and its settings template sets no such key. It counts tracked changes and untracked files as dirty even when repository config hides untracked files from git status (L161). candidates.demonstrated_gap: The layer's next_action asks for one OCI/VM candidate to compare with srt on filesystem, network and resource enforcement, state cleanup and host compatibility, and open gap 4 records no resource-limit or VM-boundary qualification. Quicksand is Microsoft's rootless, Docker-free QEMU VM sandbox for AI agents (created 2026-04-14; quick-sandbox v0.12.0 on 2026-09-14), and one API covers both hosts. accel=auto selects KVM on Linux (the WSL2 host exposes /dev/kvm) and HVF on macOS, both rated near-native. A bundled QEMU comes from the pip extras, and the WSL2 host has no system QEMU. It provides a separate guest kernel and no shared filesystem unless one is mounted. Networking is isolated by default: MOUNTS_ONLY is SLIRP restrict=on, which blocks all guest outbound traffic, and NONE is -nic none. Guest memory, cpus and disk_size are limited per sandbox, and per-sandbox qcow2 overlays support checkpoint/revert and save/load for state cleanup. srt offers none of the resource or VM-boundary properties. Limits to measure: networking is coarse (FULL is unrestricted, with no domain allowlist). QEMU is a larger attack surface than Firecracker or libkrun. The TCG fallback is 10-50x slower. Its 55 stars are no evidence either way.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the same untrusted-workload fixture on both hosts under quicksand (NetworkMode.NONE and MOUNTS_ONLY, memory=2G, cpus=2, one read-write mount) and srt 0.0.78. The fixture covers (a) the network set, including IPv6, DNS, TLS, SOCKS and remote hosts; (b) reads and writes outside the mount; (c) hostile resource workloads (fork bomb, an 8 GiB allocation, disk fill) while measuring host RSS, CPU and responsiveness; (d) leftovers after normal exit, SIGKILL of the host process and checkpoint revert; (e) cold-start and exec latency on WSL2 KVM and on the M5 Pro with HVF. Adopt quicksand as the layer's VM tier if it contains every hostile workload with no host impact and no leftovers on both hosts at acceptable latency. Reject it if nested KVM under WSL2 forces TCG or mounts fail.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20261006-vendor: Follow-up direction from the completeness critic (microsoft/WSL 3.0.1 WSLc). Verified with gh api (releases, commits, contents, issue #41492), the vendor architecture post and the GA post
candidates.demonstrated_gap: WSL containers (WSLc) are Microsoft's own VM-backed OCI runtime. They became generally available in 3.0.1 (2026-09-29), and wslc.exe and wslcsession.exe are already installed on the linux-wsl2 host. For the layer's NEXT step, WSLc is a VM-backed OCI arm that needs no nested KVM. Gaps against the current picks: (1) sandbox-runtime has no CPU or memory limits and no VM boundary (10-01 record, isolation slot role). (2) The OCI/VM default F4, rootless containers on the hosting engine, depends on cgroup delegation that microsoft/WSL#41492 reports broken on WSL 2.9.x. That issue is still open; it was last updated 2026-09-28. What WSLc offers: `wslc run` accepts --cpus, --memory, --network, --rm, --ulimit and --gpus (ContainerRunCommand.cpp L35-75). The SDK also documents session-level CPU-count and memory settings and two networking modes, NONE and BRIDGED. According to the architecture post, wslservice.exe creates each session's VM through HCS and hands it to a per-user wslcsession.exe, and each session has its own VHD. That implies a VM separate from the distro's utility VM but does not state it, so the trial must confirm it first. Differences from sandbox-runtime to measure: (a) WSLc has no egress allow-list (networking is only NONE or BRIDGED, while srt filters by domain through host proxies). (b) It has no pids-limit flag, only --ulimit. (c) No read-only root filesystem or capability arguments are defined in ArgumentDefinitions.h. Limits on any claim: Microsoft's security model says WSL 'is not a security sandbox for running untrusted code' and that containers in WSL inherit runtime and WSL properties. That applies equally to srt and to rootless containers in the distro, so no arm on this host counts as a boundary from the Windows host, and every claim here covers only the workload versus the distro. Using WSLc from inside the distro goes through a wrapper script: the GA post lists craigloewen-msft/wslc-remote, which this worker did not check. Not established: the installed WSL version (only file dates were seen), and CUDA on the RTX 4090 (the API has GPU-enable flags). WSLc does not apply to the macOS hosts; apple/container is the counterpart there.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the 10-01 frozen suite on the WSL2 host at the WSL version the trial records, with at least 30 trials per probe per arm. Arms: srt v0.0.78; F4, a rootless container on the hosting engine; and WSLc through wslc.exe, driven from the distro. Gate 0 is that a WSLc container does not share the distro's utility VM: it has a different kernel boot ID and sees none of the distro's processes or files unless they are mounted. If it fails gate 0, WSLc becomes keep_but_compare and its gap shrinks to resource limits. Metric: the pass rate over: denied out-of-tree reads and writes; denied and allowed egress (--network none and bridged); --memory and --cpus read back from the session kernel and held under memory, CPU and process-count stress; nothing left after stop and kill (processes, containers, session VMs, VHDs under %AppData%\Local\wslc\sessions); and Claude Code and Codex running unchanged inside. WSLc replaces F4 in the OCI/VM slot if its enforcement-and-cleanup pass rate beats F4's with a 95% interval on the difference that excludes zero. This includes F4 failing to start per WSL#41492. srt stays the default for tasks that need a filesystem rule set or an egress allow-list unless WSLc matches it on those probes.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: MXC is the vendor-official counterpart of the winner's engine. GitHub Docs say GitHub Copilot CLI's local sandboxing is powered by MXC, just as Claude Code builds its sandbox on @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime, but the layer has never compared the two head to head. MXC documents three things that srt 0.0.77/0.0.78 does not. (a) One versioned JSON policy runs over OS-native backends (bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) and, on Linux only, escalates to lxc and to experimental microvm (Nanvix) and hyperlight VM backends. That addresses open gap 4 (no VM-boundary qualification) without changing the policy format. (b) The bubblewrap backend installs a default-DROP egress chain in a private netns: IPv6 egress is denied outright, DNS is not opened, and ingress and hostLoopback are denied explicitly. These target gap-0 classes (IPv6, DNS) that the srt receipts do not establish. (c) v0.9.0 adds 'Stop descendants outliving teardown' cleanup. Weak points to measure rather than assume: there is no built-in hostname allowlist (MXC sends no host lists, so domain policy needs a separately configured external proxy). Copilot docs describe the macOS proxy as env-var cooperative. No resource limit beyond timeoutMs was found in the README or the bubblewrap and lxc docs. LXC filtering requires root. Every release is a prerelease (v0.9.0, 2026-09-29). The bubblewrap proxy and firewall modes need slirp4netns, which is absent on the WSL2 host.

At 1e829bf7ddf1 its README documents only dense + BM25 search fused by RRF (lines 52, 560, 632, 702, 1228), and the word 'rerank' appears only in general prose (line 1698). Release notes v1.13.3 through v1.16.0 never mention reranking. A search of its issues for 'rerank' returns only #63, a hybrid-prefetch refactor. ChunkHound is the maintained upstream integration point that was found, so no glue is needed. At 092792a93660 it defines embedding.rerank_model, rerank_url, rerank_format (cohere, tei or auto) and rerank_batch_size (configuration.md:386-390). When the provider supports reranking, its semantic search switches to 'Multi-hop + reranking' (search_service.py:72,116-118). Its docs name vLLM as the drop-in reranker server (configuration.md:828-830). It can therefore call the Cohere-compatible /rerank endpoint of the vLLM winner directly (vLLM v0.31.0 scoring.md:22-23). Its code_research tool can use the Claude Code CLI or Codex CLI as the LLM with no key, so it runs on native accounts (README:59-60,155). The cost is that it would replace SocratiCode and Qdrant rather than compose with them. It stores data in DuckDB (the stable default) or LanceDB (experimental) (configuration.md:401-402). The only restore evidence established so far, Qdrant snapshots, therefore does not carry over.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: The comparison runs at pipeline level, on the layer's frozen set of target-project questions with expected source spans (GAP0). Every arm uses the same embedder served by vLLM: nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16, the model in evidence/receipts/native-rag.json. Arms: (a) SocratiCode 1.16.0 with dense + BM25 RRF; (b) ChunkHound without rerank_model, which runs single-hop; (c) ChunkHound with rerank_format set explicitly to cohere and rerank_url pointing at a vLLM /rerank instance serving Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-4B. That model is loaded with the hf_overrides from vLLM scoring.md:85-88. Do not use ChunkHound's documented example, 'vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B --task score' (configuration.md:830). It omits those overrides and picks the size that regressed on MTEB-Code. Arm (d) holds two controls: the slot finalist llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2 and the generic bge-reranker-v2-m3. Measure paired Recall@5 and nDCG@5 against the expected spans, plus the added p50 and p95 latency per query. Pin --gpu-memory-utilization for each vLLM instance and report each model's weights plus its configured KV cache. The default reservation of about 90% would otherwise mask the real footprint. The embedder and the local generation model stay resident on the 24 GB RTX 4090 throughout. Index and watcher kill-restart recovery and DuckDB restore form an explicit cost arm. ChunkHound is refuted if arm (c) does not beat arms (a) and (b) on top-5 by a margin set before the run, or if recovery and restore cannot be re-established. SocratiCode is overturned if arm (c) wins within the latency and memory budget and recovery passes.

Sources: gh api for releases, PRs, code search and source at tag 3.0.1, plus maintainer issue comments; MicrosoftDocs and Microsoft Learn pages; the installed wsl.exe 3.0.1; and read-only host probes on NativeStack2604 (schtasks, Get-ScheduledTask, loginctl, systemctl, journalctl).
candidates.demonstrated_gap: WSL is the component that starts and stops the distro, and the winners cannot cover GAP0's unattended reboot without it. (1) Start. WSL has no setting that starts a distro when Windows boots: the installed wsl.exe 3.0.1 --help lists none, the wsl-config [boot] command runs 'when the WSL instance starts', and a keyword scan of the 2.9.11 to 3.0.2 release notes found none. Microsoft's maintainer recommends Task Scheduler running wsl.exe (#10828). The host has a Task Scheduler task 'WSL NativeStack2604 start' that the repository does not record. It uses a logon trigger with a 30 s delay, logon type Interactive, and the action C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe -d NativeStack2604 --exec /bin/true. An interactive-token task runs 'only in an existing interactive session', so a reboot with no logon (a Windows Update restart or the return of AC power) starts nothing. On 2026-10-06 the task ran at 13:48:35Z, 19 s after the distro's PID 1 (13:48:16Z). An unidentified component had already started the distro. Inside the distro the chain works: linger is on, dagu.service is enabled, and user@1000 and Dagu's scheduler were up at 13:48:27Z. (2) Stop. In the source, the guest gets at most boot.initTimeout (10 s by default) between systemctl poweroff and reboot(RB_POWER_OFF), and the host waits at most 30 s. dagu.service inherits TimeoutStopSec=90 s. One Windows restart was observed. Its systemd shutdown transaction began at 13:47:02.746Z, Dagu stopped gracefully at 13:47:02.826Z with no run evident, and user@1000 never logged as stopped. The persistent journal ends at 13:47:03.886Z with no final shutdown target, so the teardown was cut about 1.1 s in, before the guest's fallback, by an unidentified cause. The real window at a Windows restart has not been measured. PR #41688's 30 s change applies to the WSLC session VM, not the distro VM (per code search of the default branch). No receipt covers a reboot, or a stop with a run in flight.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Operator reboot drill on the linux-wsl2 workstation: 3 restarts per arm, with nobody logging on for 10 minutes.
- Arm A: the existing logon task (status quo).
- Arm B: the same action under an At startup trigger with an S4U principal (New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -LogonType S4U, no stored password).
- Arm C: no task.

For each restart, record:
- Windows LastBootUpTime, the distro's PID 1 start and the dagu.service start, from the journal;
- which component started the distro (the task's LastRunTime against PID 1);
- whether a DAG slot that fell inside the downtime runs exactly once (Dagu catch-up, #2742).

In arm B, check interop (cmd.exe /d /c ver), /mnt/c and /dev/dxg both before and after the interactive logon. With instanceIdleTimeout=-1, the instance started before logon serves the whole session, and #8643 was closed for inactivity, not fixed.

B replaces A if Dagu is running with no logon in 3/3 restarts, interop and the GPU work after logon, and no slot runs twice. If S4U fails, test TASK_LOGON_PASSWORD, or autologon with arm A.

Stop side: restart Windows while a DAG step traps SIGTERM and appends an fsync'd timestamp every 0.5 s. The last timestamp gives the real stop window. Compare boot.initTimeout 10000 against 25000 only if that window comes out near 10 s. If it stays near the observed 1.1 s, the lever is a Windows-side step that stops the distro before shutdown, which was not researched.

[general] instanceIdleTimeout set to -1 disables auto shutdown. No key starts a distro at Windows boot.

https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/blob/3.0.1/src/linux/init/init.cpp#L2829-L2846: on a terminate-instance request from the service (InitTerminateInstance, lines 2755-2774), init runs 'systemctl poweroff' in a detached thread, sleeps Config.BootInitTimeout, then calls reboot(RB_POWER_OFF).
https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/blob/3.0.1/src/linux/init/WslDistributionConfig.h#L61: BootInitTimeout = 10 * 1000. WslDistributionConfig.cpp#L56 maps it to the wsl.conf key boot.initTimeout.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
Nothing signals a power loss. A grep of docs, evidence, adoption, blueprints, catalogs and manifests finds no UPS or networkupstools reference, and whether the workstation has a UPS is unknown.

For a USB HID UPS, the vendor-native baseline is Windows itself: a HID battery miniport for USB-attached UPS devices, plus the critical battery action 'Shut Down'. That route ends in the same WSL teardown at Windows shutdown, which one restart showed cut about 1.1 s in.

NUT covers what that baseline lacks:
- network or SNMP UPSes;
- one UPS signalling several hosts, including the Macs;
- a pre-shutdown hook (upsmon SHUTDOWNCMD) that could terminate the distro, giving systemctl poweroff its initTimeout, before Windows starts its own shutdown.

GAP3 (open_gaps[3]) reads 'No container lane (Docker/Compose, Podman/Quadlet, Dev Containers) has been run against this workload, so native versus container is unmeasured.' The only executed container evidence is rootless Podman from 2026-09-23. Those receipts predate the new distro, which the 2026-10-01 review still records as not created, so they do not certify this host. The same review lists WSLc as a 'WSL3.0.1 GA currency candidate; unmeasured OCI/container workload fit'. It says a container requirement must choose among WSLc, Docker/Compose and Podman, and its next_wave is to 'compare WSLc/Docker/Podman volumes, loopback ports and shutdown recovery; restore one owned database independently'. The input JSON omits WSLc. WSLc is the host-platform vendor's own lane and is already on this host. wsl.exe --version reports 3.0.1.0, and wslc.exe, wslcsession.exe and container.exe are in C:\Program Files\WSL; none were executed. A trial therefore installs no second engine, which answers hosting-container-practice.md line 29. Architecture (deep dive):
- A per-user wslcsession.exe owns each session's VM and its storage VHD under %AppData%\Local\wslc\sessions.
- Windows-path volumes are virtiofs shares, and ports are published through the new Consommé networking.
- At tag 3.0.1 the session talks to a Docker Engine API socket (/var/run/docker.sock) inside the VM.
Limits today:
- No Compose. The GA post calls it the top request and says work on it has started, so this lane runs each container with wslc run on a network from wslc network create.
- No DOCKER_HOST endpoint (microsoft/WSL#40976 is open), so docker/compose cannot drive WSLc.
- Windows only. apple/container is the Mac counterpart and was already judged.
- No restart policy or GPU access is described in the GA post or the deep dive. Both are unknown, not shown absent.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run every arm on this host in one session: native, WSLc 3.0.1 GA, and Podman as well if the coordinator installs it for the 2026-10-01 next_wave. The 2026-09-23 Podman numbers are context only. The workload is the gap-wave3 one, unchanged: digest-pinned postgres:18.6-alpine plus the python:3.13-slim app image. On WSLc, start each container with wslc run on one wslc network. Keep PostgreSQL data on a named volume inside the session VHD, not on a Windows-path -v bind over virtiofs; the README records that an earlier Documents-directory bind mount stalled before guest boot. Measure per arm:
- build, start and ready times.
- The unchanged alembic upgrade and 12 pytest API checks, run from inside the WSL distro against Consommé-published ports. Reachability under mirrored networking is itself a check.
- Persistence across wslc container restart, session/VM shutdown (3.0.1 raised the VM termination timeout to 30 s) and a Windows reboot.
- Kill recovery. Check restart-policy support first. If WSLc has none, record a manual restart and mark kill recovery not comparable.
- pg_dump/pg_restore into an independent database, with matching row counts and checksums.
- CPU and memory under a fixed sustained load from the selected generator (Locust, if adopted).
- Cleanup of the session VHD.
WSLc is overturned if any of these hold:
- a check fails only on WSLc;
- published ports are unreachable from the distro;
- data is lost across a shutdown;
- start, recovery or resource cost is worse than the same-session Podman arm, or worse than native by a margin fixed before the run, with no offsetting gain.
If port forwarding or disk permissions misbehave, re-test on 3.0.2 once it reaches GA. candidates.demonstrated_gap:
GAP1 (open_gaps[1]) reads: 'No production authentication, hosted deployment, production load test or cloud hosting is established. The PostgreSQL build is a synthetic loopback trust-auth fixture without TLS'. The PostgreSQL clause is already partly answered. A 2026-09-23 receipt rebuilt 18.6 with OpenSSL and enforced scram-sha-256 and loopback TLS, using 'a locally generated fixture cert, not from any CA'. What remains without TLS is the HTTP edge: Next.js and FastAPI serve plain HTTP. Today that edge has no consumer. The fixture binds loopback only: next start --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 (package.json line 12), uvicorn --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18081 (serve.py line 33), and the API is reached through a same-origin rewrite to 127.0.0.1:18081 (next.config.ts line 6). WSL mirrored networking, verified 'mirrored', would expose only listeners bound beyond loopback. A TLS edge therefore presupposes a LAN-client, remote-service or production-authentication requirement, and the layer has not chosen one. That is why this is compare, not targeted. When the trigger fires, Caddy is the strongest answer verified here.
- Vendor baseline: FastAPI 0.142.2 docs prescribe one TLS Termination Proxy and name Traefik and Caddy as the two that 'can also handle certificate renewals'. Next.js 16.3.8 offers HTTPS only through next dev --experimental-https (mkcert), and documents that flag as development-only.
- Caddy issues certificates for loopback, IP and .localhost/.local/.internal/.home.arpa names from its own local CA (Smallstep libraries). It needs no ACME, DNS validation, account or credential, installs its root into the local trust store and renews intermediates automatically.
- Traefik's v3.7 TLS reference offers only ACME or user-supplied certificates. Nginx and HAProxy were not checked in this lane.
Prior record: Caddy is held as discovery_only (catalogs/landscape/independent-discovery.json /candidates/44: primary-source review, no local runtime or comparative measurement), with no refuter verdict. Pin v2.11.7 or later. 2.11.6 panicked when reverse-proxying HTTP/2 request bodies and cut off streaming/SSE responses at 60 s. The local CA 'is trusted only where the CA's root certificate is installed', and the automatic install reaches only the WSL Linux store, so the root must also be distributed to Windows and Mac clients.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: Traefik is the vendor baseline. FastAPI's HTTPS docs name it first. The FastAPI maintainers' template, at e99fbaeba3b5, runs Traefik on Docker labels with an ACME certificate resolver (--certificatesresolvers.le.acme.tlschallenge=true) for Host(...${DOMAIN}) routes. It shares Caddy's trigger: the fixture binds loopback only, and no LAN-client, remote-service or production-authentication requirement is recorded. Once the trigger fires, this requirement involves loopback and LAN names with no public domain and no new account. For that case, the v3.7 TLS-certificates reference defers automated certificates to its Let's Encrypt (ACME) page. Otherwise it accepts only user-supplied certificates through the file provider and falls back to a generated default certificate. That reference shows no built-in local CA; this is a finding from the reference, not a verified absence. On these hosts Traefik therefore needs an external certificate source, such as mkcert or a private ACME CA, to match Caddy's local HTTPS. Its own advantages are label-driven dynamic routing for a Compose or Podman lane and ACME for a public domain; neither is selected. Security cadence is active. Three high-severity advisories (request smuggling, header-sanitization bypass via trailers, path-scope bypass) were published on 2026-09-07 and patched in v3.7.13, and v3.7.14 shipped on 2026-10-06.

The repository's own runbook names the unanswered case: Claude withholds OTEL_* from subprocesses, so a worker launched through a shell is not tagged, and exact child attribution must not be inferred from logs alone (token-adoption-e2e RUNBOOK lines 97-102). The native fix is documented: with beta tracing active, Bash subprocesses inherit a W3C TRACEPARENT, and a claude -p or Agent SDK child makes its claude_code.interaction span a child of that caller span; llm_request spans carry model, effort, duration_ms, ttft_ms and token counts. The stack sets OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none and collector.yaml has no traces pipeline, trace_statements or connectors, while the otelcol-contrib on PATH (0.162.0) already bundles span_metrics and file, so no new component or second store is needed. Two cheaper native keys are also unused: prompt.id (links all events of one prompt) is in none of collector.yaml's six keep_keys lists at ecfa1127 (78-key log list at line 233), and OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_REPOSITORY (2.1.269+, default false) is unset; its vcs.* attributes would also need resource, log and metric allowlist additions, which raises a cardinality and private-repository-name question. Since then upstream added the tool.output span event (2.1.283) and fixed tool.blocked_on_user spans (2.1.288). Privacy precondition: the stack sets OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1, which puts serialized tool_input on claude_code.tool spans, so a fail-closed span allowlist must exist before any traces pipeline. Adopt traces if the child's interaction span parents under the parent's tool span, the summed span token counts per trace equal the parent's plus the child's own result usage exactly, the logs-only null path (session.id, ecosystem.task.id, prompt.id) cannot join the child to the parent task, and an extended privacy_canary.py finds 0 canaries (one placed in tool_input) in any store while its positive control leaks without the allowlist. That is low activity; the Hugging Face org is the release vehicle (granite-4.2-8b sha f8de16cdcdbc, lastModified 2026-09-04; the card gives release date August 25, 2026).

Gap against this layer's requirement and next_action ('qualify any optional model route on actual output, privacy, latency and recovery'): the Ada FP8 precision class has no qualification evidence in the repository. The current optional route, llama.cpp, has no FP8 compute path; the 2026-09-29 catalog says so itself. FP8 on Ada is recorded only as a hardware fact or an untested workstation boundary (model-currency.md L291). llm-compressor, ModelOpt and compressed-tensors appear nowhere in the repository.

Granite 4.2 8B is the cheapest way to get that evidence using vendor artifacts only:
- IBM publishes both the BF16 checkpoint and ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b-fp8 (compressed-tensors 'float-quantized', 2026-09-02) of the same dense GraniteForCausalLM model.
- The model card's vLLM route needs v0.20+ for IBM's granite_thinking_parser plugin. The built-in nemotron_v3 parser also works, and the tool parser is qwen3_coder. The pinned, already-installed vLLM 0.30.0 meets that requirement.
- vLLM lists compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 as supported on Ada (SM 8.9).
It is also the 10-02 local-generation-model co-finalist whose 24 GB co-residency check has not run. In BF16 its weights are about 16 GB by the slot's calculation, next to the embedding server's 0.16 GPU-memory reservation. The FP8 checkpoint should need roughly half the weight bytes, an estimate that has not been measured.

gpt-oss-20b ships only MXFP4, and the production Qwen3.8-27B does not fit in BF16, so neither gives a matched pair. The trial needs no toolchain, no new runtime and no new credential.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Setup: the WSL2 RTX 4090, during a window when the production generation unit is idle or stopped. Use the pinned vLLM 0.30.0 with the embedding server co-resident, a fixed context of 8192 tokens (the production route's ctx-size, not the card's 131072), and the same reasoning parser on every vLLM arm (built-in nemotron_v3). Send the slot's deciding-comparison request shapes to every arm, with the same concurrency, reasoning and output budgets.

Arms:
- A: ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b in BF16.
- B: ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b-fp8.
- B2: granite-4.2-8b with online --quantization fp8_per_tensor.
- Control: the production llama.cpp Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M route.

Measure:
- Fidelity against A: a fixed lm-evaluation-harness subset, plus a promptfoo set covering JSON-schema validity, tool selection and arguments, and multi-turn tool completion.
- Peak VRAM.
- TTFT and inter-token latency, read from vLLM's and llama.cpp's own /metrics through the existing Prometheus, so no second capture path is added.
- Privacy: no request content leaves the host.
- Recovery: restart-to-first-token after a kill. Online FP8 re-quantizes at every load; the offline artifact does not.

Decision rule, fixed before the run: B or B2 passes fidelity only with at most a 1-point absolute drop against A on the lm-eval subset and zero JSON-schema or tool-call regressions on the promptfoo set. A passing FP8 arm is adopted as the optional route or fallback only if it also beats the control's TTFT and ITL with no CPU offload and recovers within the control's restart time. Otherwise the FP8 class closes for this host.

Preregistered fit rule: if fewer than half of R's requests fit the route's context window, the route runs at a context that fits the median request; if no host can, the trial is unqualified. Ground truth is llama-server's per-request timings object (prompt_ms, predicted_per_token_ms) captured server-side for the same requests. A tool passes if it completes R on both hosts, its p50/p95 ITL is within 10% of the server's predicted_per_token_ms p50/p95, its p50/p95 TTFT is within 10% of the server's prompt_ms plus one predicted_per_token_ms (queueing is negligible at the recorded rate), and run-to-run variation stays under 5%. If only one tool passes, adopt it. candidates.demonstrated_gap:
This is the llm-tracing slot's provisional sole trace store, checked against this layer's winners. It is current: v3.20.1 was released 2026-10-02 (the same version is also tagged langwatch@v3.20.1 and langwatch-3.20.1), and the latest default-branch commit is d96113ba11e7 on 2026-10-06.

The winning pipeline stores no traces. The collector's service pipelines are logs, metrics, metrics/health and logs/sdk_receipts, and transform/privacy is wired only into the logs and metrics pipelines. Both client templates also set traces to none. Claude Code 2.1.292 ships beta spans behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1. The span names claude_code.interaction, claude_code.llm_request and claude_code.tool are present in the installed binary, and the feature is documented, but it was not executed here. LangWatch would hold that per-turn span tree.

Its own coding-agent setup (langwatch claude / langwatch instrument claude) does two things that conflict with this layer:
- It turns on four content flags: OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, TOOL_DETAILS, TOOL_CONTENT and RAW_API_BODIES.
- It exports traces, logs and metrics straight to LangWatch.
That is a second, unfiltered capture path, and it duplicates Loki and Prometheus.

The only placement without duplicate capture keeps the collector as the clients' single OTLP endpoint. The collector would get a traces pipeline with its own span privacy statements and an otlphttp exporter to /api/otel/v1/traces, which needs a new locally generated ingest key. Logs and metrics stay in Loki and Prometheus.

'Only Node.js required' still means three data services: npx @langwatch/server provisions ClickHouse, PostgreSQL and Redis itself, and the Helm baseline is about 2.8 CPU and 6.9 Gi of requests. No required trace question that the current logs-plus-metrics path cannot answer has been shown yet, so overturn_when is not met.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run the slot's own unrun deciding comparison (LangWatch vs OpenLIT vs MLflow, with Jaeger as the generic OTLP control), but through this layer's single capture path. One real Claude Code task and one real Codex task run with traces enabled, export once to the collector, and fan out to each store traces-only over otlphttp. Measure:
(a) The privacy canary extended to span attributes: zero content keys in the store with content flags off. LangWatch's own Drop policy and [SECRET] redaction count only as a second layer.
(b) Span-tree completeness and reconciliation: tool calls, subagents, durations and token/cost attributes must match the Loki events and Prometheus counters for the same session id.
(c) A named trace question, such as a subagent's share of turn latency, that Loki and Prometheus cannot answer.
(d) Total CPU, RAM and disk across ClickHouse, Postgres, Redis and the app, against the Jaeger control.
(e) Restart persistence, and collector file_storage queue replay after a store outage.
LangWatch becomes targeted only if (c) exists and it passes (a), (b) and (e) at a cost no worse than the alternatives.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
This repository is vLLM-org official. The input pin af206d991b51 is the 2026-10-05 default-branch head, not the 0.14.0 tag (2026-09-22).

The vendor-native baseline is the stack's own installed vLLM 0.30.0. It already quantizes BF16 to FP8 at load time (fp8_per_tensor / fp8_per_block) with no checkpoint and no calibration. Its hardware table lists llm-compressor FP8 W8A8 and Marlin (GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/FP4) as supported on Ada. IBM also publishes the Granite 8B FP8 artifact, so under never-self-write the Granite FP8 arm uses that artifact.

The remaining Ada-relevant gaps are:
(a) A hashable offline FP8 artifact for a model without a vendor FP8 checkpoint. The stack already pins file_sha256 for its GGUF, and an offline artifact avoids re-quantizing at every restart.
(b) W4A16 INT4 (GPTQ/AWQ via Marlin on Ada) for models FP8 cannot fit in 24 GB. RedHatAI already publishes Qwen3.8-27B-INT4, the family production serves today as a UD-Q4_K_M GGUF on llama.cpp with --n-cpu-ffn 20 partial CPU offload.
(c) Calibrated FP8 KV-cache scales, if the online FP8 arm fails on fidelity.

Every one of these needs a vLLM generation route, and llama.cpp is the optional route today. That is the critic's own fit caveat, so no gap is demonstrated now. NVFP4 and MXFP4 compute (the README's lead news) is not native on the 4090. Only the FP8 W8A8, W4A16 and FP8 KV paths apply.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: FastMCP has two gaps against mcporter on the bridge verb. (1) Trace context across the bridge. The 2026-07-28 revision carries W3C traceparent/tracestate in _meta (SEP-414). Claude Code exports TRACEPARENT to Bash-tool subprocesses when OTel tracing is enabled. For mcporter, 'traceparent' was not found in GitHub code search of openclaw/mcporter, and its CHANGELOG at v0.14.2 has no trace-context entry. A traced agent-to-bridge-to-server call therefore loses its parent at the bridge. FastMCP documents client-side spans (`tools/call ... (CLIENT)`) and trace-context propagation on outbound requests in _meta. Its telemetry docs say native mode propagates, and propagation_only mode states that 'Outbound requests still carry traceparent and tracestate in _meta'. For the `fastmcp call` CLI, injection needs an OTel SDK, and pickup of an inherited TRACEPARENT is unverified; that is the trial's first measurement. (2) The bridge head-to-head on record (receipts 6 and 12, 2026-09-23) has a single third-party arm, wong2/mcp-cli 2.0.0, which is now stale (0 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08). Since 3.0.0, FastMCP has shipped an MCP client CLI covering the same verbs: `fastmcp list` (tools, resources and prompts; --input-schema/--output-schema; --json; --auth oauth|bearer|none), `fastmcp call` (schema-driven coercion, --json) and `fastmcp discover --source claude-code`. FastMCP 4.0.0 is built on the 2026-07-28 revision and Python SDK v2, and negotiates the best mutual protocol era by default (#4572). All 8 GitHub advisories against it are fixed in 3.2.0 or earlier, so none affects 4.0.11. The CLI page read states no Horizon (paid hosting) requirement; v4.0.0 adds a Horizon auth client (#4785). This is a lighter local arm for the same trace-context trial as today's agentgateway targeted proposal, so the two can run together.

This repository fills two gaps the winners leave open. (1) Open gap 1: skfolio 1.4.12 WalkForward exposes only purged_size (default 0) and has no embargo parameter, so development labels can cross fold boundaries. ml4t-diagnostic ships purged walk-forward, combinatorial/CPCV and calendar-aware splitters (splitters/walk_forward.py, combinatorial.py, cpcv, calendar.py, group_isolation.py). candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run only after decision 7's gate opens, that is, once a prediction contract is written and an executable economic oracle is qualified. Use the convergence-20260926 spec with four arms: scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingRegressor (control), LightGBM 4.7.0, XGBoost 3.4.1 (PyPI) and CatBoost 1.2.10. Run them on the frozen WalkForward folds in blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/ with an identical factor panel and forward-return target. Conditions:
- Preregister before any output is seen (decision 7 item 5).
- Set purge at least equal to the label horizon, with a nonzero embargo (open gap 1; evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/us-equities__research-factors-ml/1-purge-embargo-fold-boundary.json).
- Give every arm the same fixed tuning budget.
- Score development-fold IC and rank-IC, CPU wall-clock against HGBR (GPU timings reported separately), and reserved-segment Sharpe net of costs computed by the oracle, deflated for N=4 arms, with MinTRL.
Adopt LightGBM only if it beats HGBR outside noise at comparable wall-clock. Scikit-learn stays in any of three cases: parity, an HGBR win, or a reserved segment too short to resolve the difference (open gap 0 records only 11 reserved episodes).

Vendor-pass crowding. 14 of 97 proposal slots went to anthropics/claude-code or openai/codex, across 10 of 13 layers; at least one lane refuted 10 of those 14. Add host-platform and north-star vendor orgs to the vendor pass.

GitHub-only canonical form. Repositories of the form https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> cannot represent Hugging Face models. All 8 semantic-rag proposals were runtimes or tools, with 0 models. Model currency here came only from a separate Hugging Face API pass (huggingface.co/api/models?author=<org>&sort=createdAt). Make that pass a standing sweep step for the model slots.

Refuter asymmetry. Claude fit-refuted 61 proposals and gpt6 43. Claude was stricter in workers (6 vs 2), quality-evaluation (6 vs 2), semantic-rag (6 vs 2) and isolation (4 vs 1). gpt6 was stricter in hosting-services (7 vs 3). Survival requires both lanes, so in each layer the stricter lane decides. Three layers ended with zero surviving targeted or keep proposals: agent-sdks, observation-inference and hosting-services.

Facts refuted. 9 proposals had facts refuted, 6 of them vendor-org repositories: modelcontextprotocol/conformance, docker/mcp-registry, microsoft/mxc, ggml-org/llama.cpp, anthropics/defending-code-reference-harness and QwenLM/qwen-code. Adversarial verification per layer: a facts/identity refuter (claude-opus-5-5, effort max) and two fit/standing refuters (claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6-astra, effort max), each defaulting to refuted, within 8 web searches, 10 page fetches and 30 GitHub API calls; a candidate survives only when no refuter refutes it, and a missing vote counts as refuted.

counts.trading_layers_note: trading_layers counts only taxonomy layers with at least one selected entry, unlike foundation_layers (which counts every row); trading[] itself always has one row per taxonomy id, so len(manifest["trading"]) can exceed trading_layers whenever a taxonomy layer happens to have zero selected entries
counts.pin_status_note: pins_behind_upstream counts the generator's computed pin fields; pins_behind_upstream_by_review_status splits those rows by published review_status. A row's review_status is pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] only when its computed pin_behind_upstream is true, so review_status_pin_behind_upstream equals the pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] share of that split; a lane pin claim the computed fields contradict is published as pin_status_disputed[_unverified] (the lane's claim in disputed_lane_status and the row evidence) or, on an OS-package pin, distro_managed
counts.pins_behind_note: components with a commit-pinned version (a parenthetical hash), a non-GitHub repository, or an OS-distribution package pin (matched by an -Nubuntu/-Ndeb/+debN pin suffix, or by id via --os-package-ids, e.g. systemd even though its own repository is on GitHub) are excluded from the pin-vs-upstream comparison rather than counted either way
counts.pins_not_compared_note: rows whose pin the generator could not compare with upstream (the exclusions above, plus a pin or upstream latest with no parseable version, reason unversioned) carry pin_behind_upstream null and pin_comparison not_compared, never a definite false
counts.lane_groupings_note: every foundation/trading-scoped count above (candidates_total, candidates_by_disposition, components_confirmed, pins_behind_upstream, pins_behind_upstream_unique_components) is computed from all_rows = manifest['foundation'] + manifest['trading'] only, and so excludes lane_groupings[].selected rows the same way it excludes lane_groupings[].candidates; candidates inside lane_groupings (a review-lane grouping id outside the foundation/taxonomy baseline, e.g. an awesome-list survey) are counted only in lane_grouping_candidates; counts.citation_review (computed below, by apply_citation_review) is the same way scoped -- its rows_flagged/attached only ever count a foundation/trading row, never a lane_groupings[].selected row, since apply_citation_review only walks manifest['foundation'] and manifest['trading']
